topic: A Bengaluru startup wants to heat plasma
hook: A Bengaluru startup wants to heat plasma to *100 million °C*
hook_b: India's first private fusion reactor: blueprint by *2027*?
tldr: Pranos Fusion aims to finalise designs for PRANIK, India's first privately built tokamak, by 2027.

beats.what: Bengaluru's Pranos Fusion built PRAGYA, a small tokamak, as a step to a bigger reactor.
beats.why: Fusion needs no uranium and has almost no runaway risk, the founders say.
beats.care: Deep-tech jobs are growing; fusion electricity is still years away, the CEO says.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: A tokamak is a doughnut-shaped reactor where magnets hold superheated plasma off the walls. Fusion needs fuel at around 100 million °C. CEO Shaurya Kaushal says the PRANIK blueprint should be final by 2027; making electricity is 'a further step away'. Co-founder Roshan George says India already produces plenty of deuterium. The startup is incubated at the Institute of Plasma Research and JNCASR, Bengaluru. Funding was not in the report.

cards.q: Should India bet big on fusion power?

cards.why: A tokamak uses magnets to hold superheated plasma in a doughnut shape.

insight: Pranos Fusion has already built a small test tokamak, PRAGYA, to trial magnets and plasma control.

learn.t: Fusion joins light atoms (like hydrogen) to release energy; today's nuclear plants split heavy atoms (fission).
